title: Kissed Polish White Chocolate Cobbler
description: A sweet and flaky Polish dessert featuring white chocolate chips and kombu-cold-extract, perfect for kids and those following a shojin diet.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, cold butter, and sugar until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the kombu-cold-extract and mix until the dough comes together.
Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and gently knead until smooth.
Roll the dough out into a circle that is about 1/4-inch thick.
Transfer the dough to a 9-inch cast-iron skillet or round cake pan.
In a small bowl, whisk together the eggs and vanilla extract.
Pour the egg mixture over the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Sprinkle the white chocolate chips over the top of the dough.
Bake the cobbler for 30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbly.
Reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is set.
Remove the cobbler from the oven and let it cool for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Serve warm, topped with additional raspberry jam if desired.
